table_title: For each of ten major music genres (Jazz, Country, Rock, Electronic, Heavy metal, Soul, Punk rock, Hip hop, Grunge, Pop), name the album most prominently described as the genre's foundational or landmark album in the genre's Wikipedia article, the artist who recorded it, and its year of release.
db_analog: SELECT g.genre_name AS genre, a.album_title AS landmark_album, a.artist_name AS artist, a.release_year AS year_of_release FROM music_genres g JOIN landmark_album_per_genre l ON l.genre_id = g.id JOIN albums a ON a.id = l.album_id WHERE g.is_major = TRUE AND l.foregrounded_in_genre_article = TRUE ORDER BY a.release_year ASC, g.genre_name ASC
temporal_note: Wikipedia per-genre articles for 10 major music genres + 10 per-album articles (one per chosen landmark album), all accessed 2026-05-12. The universe is 10 major music genres — Jazz, Country music, Rock music, Electronic music, Heavy metal music, Soul music, Punk rock, Hip hop music, Grunge, Pop music — chosen as a curator subset of the major recorded-music genres covered by Wikipedia. Excluded after cycle-1 + cycle-2 audit-driven research: Blues and Folk (their Wikipedia genre articles do not foreground any single studio landmark album, instead treating each tradition as pre-LP-era field-recording archives); Reggae (Wikipedia article foregrounds Bob Marley as an artist but does not name any single Marley studio album in body text — Catch a Fire appears only in references); Funk (article foregrounds artists and singles, not LPs); Disco (article foregrounds Saturday Night Fever soundtrack, which is a multi-artist compilation disqualified under the 'single studio or live album' rule); Rhythm and blues (singles-era genre, no LP foregrounded). Grunge was added in cycle-2 to replace Reggae (its article strongly foregrounds Nirvana's Nevermind 1991 as the genre-defining mainstream-breakthrough album). For each genre the staged Landmark Album is the album most prominently described in the genre's Wikipedia article as foundational, era-defining, or genre-defining (with the most narrative emphasis in lead or history-section position); ties are broken by precedence of mention in article structure. All facts are stable historical record (album releases are decades old; the qualitative landmark-album judgment is a curator call within each genre's Wikipedia framing).
_extraction_notes: Qualitative instance: tests whether the model can identify a genre's canonical foundational album per Wikipedia genre-article framing. Universe = 10 major music genres × 1 landmark album each = 10 rows. Schema: 4 cols (Genre PK + Landmark Album + Artist + Year of Release numeric). Universe is curator-supplemented (10 of N possible genres; 6 genres excluded after cycle-1 + cycle-2 audit-verified research: Blues + Folk (pre-LP-era field-recording traditions; only compilations cited), Reggae (Wikipedia article foregrounds Bob Marley as artist but no Marley studio album in body text — Catch a Fire only in references), Funk (article foregrounds artists + singles like 'Cold Sweat', not LPs), Disco (Saturday Night Fever soundtrack is multi-artist compilation, disqualified), Rhythm and blues (singles-era genre; no LP foregrounded). Full per-genre exclusion rationale in proposed_supplements. Pop music is included but has a weak landmark signal: Britney Spears 'Blackout' (2007) is the only album named in the Pop article, but as a stylistic-shift epitomization rather than a genre-defining landmark — flagged in open_questions. Sort order: Year of Release ASC primary, Genre ASC secondary. Year range: 1959 (Kind of Blue) to 2007 (Blackout). Cycles 1+2+3 + Fields-Medal-cycles + painters-cycle + extinctions-cycles + deserts-cycles + tennis-cycles lessons applied upfront: (a) single PK on Genre (canonical Wikipedia article title for 9 of 10 genres; 'Hip hop music' is a disambiguating redirect-source to the broader 'Hip-hop' article); (b) per-row data sourced from 2 articles each (per-genre + per-album), 20 URLs total; (c) explicit selection rule for Landmark Album ('most prominently described in the genre's Wikipedia article as foundational/landmark, with the most narrative emphasis; ties broken by precedence in article structure'); (d) curator-supplemented universe (10 of N possible major genres) with explicit per-genre exclusion rationale for Blues/Folk/Reggae/Funk/Disco/Rhythm and blues documented in proposed_supplements; (e) Pop music's weak landmark signal documented as audit-known-ambiguity in open_questions; (f) operation_type 'join' (genre ⋈ album-of-the-genre).
